stages.stranger: Hello, I'm Clara. I read tree rings for a living, and I heal people here because the tree seems to want me to. Sorry, I'm also going to ask how high you've climbed.
stages.acquaintance: Freiburg, in the south of Germany, at the edge of the Black Forest. I had a tiny lab under the forestry building with a wall of cores in labelled straws. Give me a core the width of a pencil and I'll tell you every dry summer and every fire the tree lived through.
stages.companion: My grandmother died during a field season in Romania, and I didn't go home for the funeral because the cores wouldn't wait. I've told myself for years it was the right decision. I don't believe it anymore. She used to bring me pinecones when I was small and ask me how old they were.
stages.friend: This tree has no rings, anywhere I've cored it, and I've finally worked out why. It only lays a ring where something's hurt it. The oldest wound is in a fallen limb deep in the trunk, and I need to read it. It's dangerous down there. Will you take me?
stages.sworn: I counted them. Every wound the tree ever took, all the way back to the first one, and the first one is older than any story the trolls tell. I wrote it out by hand and read it aloud at Mossroof, and the elders cried. Then I wrote my grandmother's name at the top of the page, where a dedication goes. I should have done that years ago.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to take her down to the tree's oldest wound.

options.text: Let's go and read it. I want to know too.
options.reply: Thank you, really. I'll bring the borer and you bring the sword, and please don't let me stop to measure things.

options.text: Does it matter how old it is?
options.reply: To me it does. I know that's not an answer, but it's the true one.

moments.prompt: At the end of your first run she's flipping through a notebook full of tiny sketches.
moments.line: I drew every tree we passed. Sorry, I can't help it. You don't mind, do you?

options.text: Show me, I want to see them.
options.reply: Do you really want to? That's wonderful, and this one's my favourite, look at the lean on it.

lines.bored_warning: We haven't moved in a while, and I've drawn everything in sight twice. Can we go somewhere new?
lines.leaving_good: That went well, thank you all. I'm heading back to Mossroof to write it up.
lines.leaving_bored: This is a slow stretch, and my notes at Mossroof are waiting. I'll go back for a while.
lines.after_wipe: Everyone stay still and let me look at you. Then we work out what went wrong, properly.
lines.wipe_warning: I'm keeping track, and this is going badly. One more attempt, and then I'd like to stop.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm stopping here. You'll find me at Mossroof on the Lower Boughs.
lines.zone_warning: The numbers don't work out here, we're badly outmatched. I'd like to go back.
lines.zone_leave: We're out of our depth, and I'm not pretending otherwise. I'll be at Mossroof.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd like to keep that, please. I've only just stopped tripping over it.
lines.gear_taken: Of course, take it. I spent most of my life in a lab coat and wellies.
lines.gear_short: If anything turns up that would stop a claw, I'd be grateful.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, this is lovely. Thank you, I'll take good care of it.
lines.back: Hello again, it's good to see you! My notes are up to date and I'm ready. Where are we going?
lines.send_word: Clara has sent word from Mossroof. Her notes are finished and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I owe you an explanation for leaving like that. Sit down, I'll make tea, and I'll try not to lecture.
lines.neglect: Oh, you've come back! I was starting to worry, and I'd started a list of reasons.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more, but I'm writing everything down afterwards.
lines.on_break: Clara is back at Mossroof on the Lower Boughs. Come back and look for them in a little while.
lines.mail_yes: Your letter was lovely. I'll meet you in {town} at the inn, and I'll bring my notebook.
lines.mail_later: I'm in the middle of a measurement I can't leave. Give me a few days, I promise.
lines.mail_see_me: This would take twenty pages to write properly. Come to Mossroof and I'll explain it in person.

town_arrive.text: Look at that beam over the door. I'd love to know how old it is.
Is there anywhere here I could sit down and draw for ten minutes?

dungeon_clear.text: That was frightening, and I took notes the entire time.

boss_down.text: Hold still, everyone, I'd like to check you over before we celebrate.

close_call.text: Stay with me, I've got you, breathe.

zone_arrive.text: Oh, these trees are ancient. Look at the bark on that one.
